aspects.says: A pattern switch throws NullPointerException on null unless it has case null, because default does not match null.
basis: section:Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

aspects.says: A plain type pattern placed before a guarded pattern of the same type makes the guarded case unreachable, which the compiler rejects.
basis: section:Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

aspects.says: getFirst() and getLast() throw NoSuchElementException on an empty collection.
The Foreign Function and Memory API, a third preview in Java 21 and final in Java 22, replaces JNI for native interop.
aspects.reason: a preview API that needs native code and --enable-preview; incidental to this page's practices

aspects.says: Among guarded cases the most specific comes first, since the first case whose pattern and guard match wins.
Virtual threads help I/O-bound work and bring no gain to CPU-bound work, which belongs on a platform thread pool.
basis: section:Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

aspects.says: Blocking inside synchronized pins a virtual thread to its carrier in Java 21, where a ReentrantLock lets it unmount.
basis: section:Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them
aspects.reason: carrier pinning is a scheduling property no graded test can observe deterministically; virtual threads have their own module (26)

aspects.says: A record pattern with var components matches even when a reference component is null.
aspects.reason: incidental detail, not practised; the segments practice deconstructs int components only

aspects.says: Record patterns deconstruct a record's components, and nest to reach into components that are records themselves.
basis: section:Q3: What are record patterns and how do they enable nested deconstruction?

aspects.says: reversed() returns a view of the collection, not a copy.
basis: section:Q5: What are sequenced collections and why were they added?

aspects.says: A switch over a sealed type that covers every permitted subtype needs no default.
aspects.reason: a compile-time check with no runtime behaviour to grade; sealed hierarchies are practised in module 10

aspects.says: SequencedCollection gives lists, deques, LinkedHashSet and TreeSet the same getFirst, getLast and reversed methods.
basis: section:Q5: What are sequenced collections and why were they added?

aspects.says: SequencedMap adds firstEntry, lastEntry and reversed to LinkedHashMap and TreeMap.
basis: section:Q5: What are sequenced collections and why were they added?
aspects.reason: the same first, last and reversed idea the collection practice covers; incidental detail, not practised separately

aspects.says: Structured concurrency bounds subtasks by a block, which a virtual-thread-per-task executor in try-with-resources imitates by waiting for every task on close.
basis: section:Q4: What is structured concurrency and why is it important?

aspects.says: A switch matches any object by type patterns with when guards, and the first matching case wins.
basis: section:Q2: Explain pattern matching for switch with examples of guarded patterns and null handling.

aspects.says: ThreadLocal is costly with millions of virtual threads, and ScopedValue (a preview) is its replacement.
aspects.reason: ScopedValue is a preview API the practices cannot compile without --enable-preview, and the memory cost is not observable in a test

aspects.says: Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor() and Thread.ofVirtual() create virtual threads, which isVirtual() reports.
